bracket: [Textbook misprint: the book's printed working sets \(l = 3\dfrac{\lambda}{2}\), which treats the string as fixed at BOTH ends, but this string is fixed at one end and driven at its FREE end. A free end is an antinode, so three complete loops are followed by a quarter wavelength: \(l = \dfrac{7\lambda}{4}\), \(\lambda = 0.60\) m and \(\text{v} = 9.00\ \text{m s}^{-1}\), not the printed \(10.50\ \text{m s}^{-1}\). The book itself treats the same set-up (a string fixed at one end, driven at 15 Hz at its free end) this way in Exercise Q.19, with the hint "Remember that the free end is an antinode". The working below has been corrected.]
